- [react--v18.2.0:packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberWorkLoop.old.js?L1525-L1555](/r/github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberWorkLoop.old.js?L1525-L1555) - Render work handles thrown promises, marks the component suspended, and schedules the boundary retry.
- [react--v18.2.0:packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberBeginWork.old.js?L320-L355](/r/github.com/sg-evals/react--v18.2.0/-/blob/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberBeginWork.old.js?L320-L355) - `forceUnmountCurrentAndReconcile()` is the explicit path that discards the current child tree and remounts it when reconciliation requires replacement.

Why the global bump is transitive: Relay stores a `"global"` invalidation epoch in every `InvalidationState`; a store invalidation changes that epoch and the notification path can invoke subscribers even when none of their specific IDs were invalidated. Any resulting Relay hook update re-runs the component. If `useFragment`/`useLazyLoadQuery` observes data now considered stale or pending, it can throw a wakeable; React’s `throwException()` marks the nearest Suspense boundary with capture state, and `updateSuspenseComponent()` switches to the fallback. The fallback/primary branch transition unmounts the visible subtree, so its client state is lost even though the originally invalidated record was not directly read by that subtree.
